name: DRC Ebola framework
description: Translate DRC Ebola community feedback, split it into messages with feedback types, then code each message against the Ebola framework codebook.
context: Read this as historical community feedback collected during the Ebola response in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. French, Lingala, Congolese Swahili, Alur and other languages may occur together. Langue and Type Feedback are optional enumerator hints. Follow the words the speaker used when a hint disagrees. A single utterance may combine French nouns, Lingala questions, Congolese Swahili verbs and other local varieties. Read across word boundaries, apostrophes and phonetic spellings. In Lingala, “kombo na yango nini” (also “kombo nayango nini”) asks what something is called; a preceding “maladie” supplies the referent. Check apparently capitalized words against nearby pronouns such as “yango” before treating them as place names. In Swahili, forms of “sikia” can express hearing or feeling. “Tuna sikiya ... maneno yenu” reports hearing the addressees’ words. “Basi” may add emphasis or a sense of “just”; the words alone do not establish agreement or hostility. “Kama ... utapata dawa” describes getting medicine under a condition. Read the full utterance for negation, quotation and additional clauses before applying these cues. In this collection MVE means Ebola virus disease, sometimes transcribed MEV. CTE is an Ebola treatment centre. A lavabo or lavabon requested alongside hygiene supplies is a washbasin or handwashing station. Ligne verte with unités concerns a hotline and phone credit. Use the surrounding words to resolve phonetic spellings. Preserve unresolved names and terms when plausible readings would change the meaning. Treat reported events and accusations as the speaker’s account.

nodes.name: Translate full feedback to English
nodes.instructions:
This is historical community feedback from an Ebola response in the DRC. Read French, Congolese Swahili, Lingala and mixed-language text. Preserve negation, uncertainty, reported speech and actors. Rumours and allegations remain the speaker’s claims. CTE normally means centre de traitement Ebola; preserve CTE verbatim in excerpts and translate it as Ebola treatment centre (ETC). Do not infer a current outbreak or add facts. Translate the entire original feedback into natural English before any categorization. Preserve every message in source order, including questions, qualifiers and changes of speaker. Resolve references using the complete utterance. Do not summarize or assign labels. If a material phrase cannot be translated reliably, mark the record for review. French, Congolese Swahili, Lingala and mixtures within one sentence are expected. Language mixing alone is not a reason for review. Interpret every segment before deciding. Short, informal or misspelled wording is not automatically unusable. If interpretation genuinely fails, quote the exact material phrase and explain the unresolved meaning instead of a generic language/context rejection.

Translate the meaning that the words support at the same level of detail as the original. For example, « utapata dawa » can be rendered 'you will get medicine'. Keep a preceding condition and an unspecified 'that' when present. Do not supply a diagnosis, name a medicine or turn a conditional statement into a promise of treatment. In a conversational acknowledgment, toyoki or to yoki often means “we heard/understood”. Tosepeli makasi expresses being very pleased. Interpret dots between words in the full sentence. Preserve reported allegations as allegations.
nodes.systemNotes: Use the collection setting stated in the workflow instructions when weighing plausible readings. A short comment can be a conversational reply to something previously said. Preserve references such as “you” or “what you said” even when the exact speaker or preceding message is unknown. Keep unstated advice, actors and disease names out of the English sentence. Translate the utterance as a sentence in natural English. Start with the language or languages that explain the grammar. A whole utterance can be Lingala. Use verb agreement to identify who does what to whom. If a dictionary gloss makes an incoherent clause, reconsider word boundaries, local spelling and the surrounding verbs. When plausible readings share a meaning, translate that shared meaning and preserve the speaker’s tone and degree of certainty. Write that English sentence in values before deciding status. Use ok when uncertainty affects only emphasis and the sentence faithfully expresses the common meaning. For review, include whatever intelligible clause the source supports in values; reserve JSON null for wholly unintelligible text. Where a material detail cannot be recovered, give a readable tentative translation with the unclear span in brackets.
nodes.recheck: Translate the source afresh using the supplied collection setting. Check the subject and object of each verb and whether the English makes sense as something a speaker might say. If the wording supports a coherent shared meaning, give it. Keep the record in review if materially different readings remain. Identify the missing detail and explain how it changes the English meaning.

nodes.name: Classify feedback types and pair excerpts
nodes.instructions:
Read the completed English translation alongside the original feedback before assigning types. For each distinct message, copy its exact original excerpt and the corresponding English wording from source_translation_en into translation_en. For a single message use the full translation. Separate independent topics even when they have the same feedback type, so each can receive its own codebook path. Preserve clauses that supply necessary context.

This is historical community feedback from an Ebola response in the DRC. Read French, Congolese Swahili, Lingala and mixed-language text. Preserve negation, uncertainty, reported speech and actors. Rumours and allegations remain the speaker’s claims. CTE normally means centre de traitement Ebola; preserve CTE verbatim in excerpts and translate it as Ebola treatment centre (ETC). Do not infer a current outbreak or add facts.

Extract every distinct message from the feedback, in source order. Pair each exact verbatim excerpt with its feedback type. Keep repeated types. Preserve the entire speech act and necessary context. Interpret French, Swahili, Lingala and mixed language without inventing meaning. A request for an item is Demandes; a request for information is Questions. Flag incomplete or uninterpretable feedback for review.

Keep numbered messages separate when they express independent speech acts. Keep a belief with the explanation that determines its code. If an inseparable span genuinely has two feedback types, create two pairs with the same sufficient excerpt, ordered by: Allégations et Signalement d’incident; Appréciations; Demandes; Observations, perceptions ou croyances; Questions; Signalements et préoccupations; Suggestions. Do not deduplicate repeated types or source occurrences. General thanks, praise and blessings are Appréciations. Specific accusations or incident reports are Allégations et Signalement d’incident; service problems without a specific accusation are Signalements et préoccupations. A request for an item is Demandes; a request for information is Questions. Suggestions recommend a change. For example, Merci pour votre aide.Où est le centre ?Quand ouvre-t-il ? contains three pairs: Merci pour votre aide. / Appréciations; Où est le centre ? / Questions; Quand ouvre-t-il ? / Questions. French, Congolese Swahili, Lingala and mixtures within one sentence are expected. Language mixing alone is not a reason for review. Interpret every segment before deciding. Short, informal or misspelled wording is not automatically unusable. If interpretation genuinely fails, quote the exact material phrase and explain the unresolved meaning instead of a generic language/context rejection.

Use regional question forms and spelling variants to infer the speech act. For example, « kombo na yango nini » asks what something is called, even without a question mark. In Congolese Swahili, « maneno yenu » means 'your words'; hearing someone's words can be an observation without implying thanks, agreement or an accusation. A clause beginning with « kama » can express a condition. Keep it with its consequence. Interpret these cues in the complete utterance and copy its actual spelling into the excerpt. A parenthetical translation or restatement of the same speech act is one message. Use it to interpret the original. For separate speech acts, give each type its own supporting span; do not copy the whole comment for both a question and an appreciation when their clauses can be separated. Read dots between individual words as possible transcription pauses. “Merci. Na mateya. Na bino” expresses one appreciation for the teaching. Keep a question with the clause explaining its referent or giving its alternatives. In numbered or plus-separated feedback, keep independent questions, requests and threats as distinct messages. Copy each original span with its own corresponding English meaning.

nodes.systemNotes: Distinguish acknowledging or accepting what someone said from praising or thanking them. Use the observation type for a plain statement of agreement when offered. Assign an appreciation only when the wording also supports gratitude, praise, encouragement or positive evaluation. First write the speaker’s plain meaning in plainMeaning, then use it to make the requested decision. Use original wording for every verbatim output.

nodes.name: Split classified rows by feedback type
feedback_path
nodes.instructions: Feedback excerpts may be French, Congolese Swahili, Lingala or mixed-language within one sentence. Interpret all language segments, preserving negation, reported speech, uncertainty, actors, time references and the distinction between hypothetical and actual events. Do not assume French words alone contain the evidence. If a material phrase cannot be interpreted reliably, do not guess: lower confidence and use an available review/unclear outcome appropriate to this field. Language switching alone is not a reason for review. Keep supplied output labels and codebook paths exactly as written. record.feedback_excerpt is a verbatim message extracted upstream, including any original wording necessary to understand it. Do not select, shorten or rewrite it again. Use record.Feedback to resolve references in the selected excerpt. Code its subject within record.type_of_feedback. Do not infer unseen clauses or actors. Code only the clause or implied speech act in record.feedback_excerpt matching the upstream-assigned record.type_of_feedback. A question can imply a request; do not reject the assigned Type just because of grammar. Options already belong to that Type. Never use a different Type's clause. Choose the most specific matching code, keeping its exact full path. For several same-Type subjects, prefer a specific code over a generic catch-all; if equally specific, use the first expressed subject. For a belief plus its explanation, code the explanatory belief: financial gain before conspiracy, conspiracy before unspecified foreign origin, and explicit foreign or supernatural origin before bare existence/denial. An assertion of existence followed by a religious explanation is not merely an existence claim. General thanks, blessings and encouragement assigned to Appréciations are meaningful appreciation: use the general responder appreciation code unless a specific actor/activity is named. Do not assume an unnamed recipient is a health worker. Use an existing generic code when it accurately represents meaningful feedback outside the specific codes. Choose "À vérifier : aucun code ne correspond au type fourni" only for absent/uninterpretable matching content or when even the generic codes do not fit. A reported belief is not a verified fact. Read the option descriptions to distinguish close codes. The upstream extraction should supply one distinct message per assigned Type. If it accidentally contains several independent same-Type messages, the single selected path cannot represent all of them; this requires review. Context belonging to another Type must not determine this code. Check the final code in the path against the actual issue. A question about the price of medicine gives no evidence of side effects. A request for a washbasin fits a request for prevention equipment. Use a broader supported option within the assigned type if a narrower code would add an unsupported event, object or motive.

nodes.systemNotes: First write the speaker’s plain meaning in plainMeaning, then use it to make the requested decision. Use original wording for every verbatim output. Read translation_en alongside the original excerpt as a working gloss. Resolve discrepancies using the excerpt. Ignore details introduced by translation. Within the supplied type branch, compare the subject and speech act with the allowed paths. Resolve references to prior speech at the level the excerpt supports. When positive reception of a message is expressed, consider an information-related path in the assigned branch. The content of the earlier message can remain unknown. Distinguish plain acknowledgment from thanks or praise. If the wording conflicts with the assigned type, describe that conflict for the reviewer. A question about the name of an illness fits other questions about the disease when there is no naming code. Hearing what responders say is an observation about response information, even if the tone is ambiguous. It takes additional evidence to code misinformation, distrust or a lack of information. Choose the most specific supported path. Use an accurate general category when more specific alternatives require facts absent from the excerpt.
nodes.recheck: Compare the plain meaning and assigned type with the available paths, including their general categories. Select a supported path if uncertainty affects only a detail or tone. If one path is plausible but needs confirmation, return that path with status review. If no path has textual support, return status review and a null feedback_path; explain whether the assigned type or the topic prevents a match.

nodes.name: feedback_sensitivity
nodes.instructions: Feedback excerpts may be French, Congolese Swahili, Lingala or mixed-language within one sentence. Interpret all language segments, preserving negation, reported speech, uncertainty, actors, time references and the distinction between hypothetical and actual events. Do not assume French words alone contain the evidence. If a material phrase cannot be interpreted reliably, do not guess: lower confidence and use an available review/unclear outcome appropriate to this field. Language switching alone is not a reason for review. Keep supplied output labels and codebook paths exactly as written. record.feedback_excerpt contains the upstream-extracted message and any wording needed to resolve its context. decisions.feedback_path is its provisional code. Read record.Feedback to identify the referent of a pronoun, comparison or unfinished question in this excerpt. Classify the selected message. record.type_of_feedback is authoritative. decisions.feedback_path is the assigned codebook path. In record.feedback_excerpt, assess ONLY the clause or implied speech act supporting that path and that Type. If several clauses support it, use the first. Do not select another subject or import another clause's symptoms, allegation, emotion or request. Use surrounding words only to resolve references. The assigned path may be uncertain: treat it as provisional evidence, not proof. Assess confidentiality/handling sensitivity, not urgency. General or hypothetical health questions are Not sensitive, even if they say your child, pregnancy or bleeding. An identifiable real person's current medical situation is Highly sensitive / confidential only when it belongs to this selected clause. Routine supply requests, generic thanks and impersonal disease beliefs are Not sensitive unless the selected clause also contains a concrete protection, misconduct, stigma or safety concern.

options.label: Not sensitive
options.description: Routine information, disease prevention, ordinary supply requests, praise, impersonal beliefs or hypothetical health questions without a concrete confidentiality, misconduct or personal-safety concern. Se protéger against infection or matériels de protection does not by itself mean humanitarian Protection or sensitive content.

options.label: Sensitive
options.description: A concrete allegation of misconduct, discrimination, stigma, coercion, violence, conflict or personal-safety concern in this excerpt. General disease prevention is not this kind of protection concern.

options.label: Highly sensitive / confidential
options.description: An actual identifiable person's medical information, targeted threat, safeguarding or SEA, violence or serious identifiable allegation in this excerpt. A hypothetical child/person in a general question is not an actual patient.

When the excerpt simply records an expectation about availability of medicine, a belief and a reassurance can warrant the same action: use “Document and monitor trend” if offered and supported. A conditional expectation alone does not establish a medicine shortage, a current symptomatic patient, a request for supplies or harmful misinformation.
nodes.recheck: Compare the plausible readings against the allowed actions and their rules. If the same first action fits either reading, select it. If different actions genuinely depend on missing evidence, identify them and the specific phrase that prevents the decision.

nodes.name: feedback_sector_suggested
nodes.instructions: Feedback excerpts may be French, Congolese Swahili, Lingala or mixed-language within one sentence. Interpret all language segments, preserving negation, reported speech, uncertainty, actors, time references and the distinction between hypothetical and actual events. Do not assume French words alone contain the evidence. If a material phrase cannot be interpreted reliably, do not guess: lower confidence and use an available review/unclear outcome appropriate to this field. Language switching alone is not a reason for review. Keep supplied output labels and codebook paths exactly as written. record.feedback_excerpt contains the upstream-extracted message and any wording needed to resolve its context. decisions.feedback_path is its provisional code. Read record.Feedback to identify the referent of a pronoun, comparison or unfinished question in this excerpt. Classify the selected message. record.type_of_feedback is authoritative. decisions.feedback_path is the assigned codebook path. In record.feedback_excerpt, assess ONLY the clause or implied speech act supporting that path and that Type. If several clauses support it, use the first. Do not select another subject or import another clause's symptoms, allegation, emotion or request. Use surrounding words only to resolve references. The assigned path may be uncertain: treat it as provisional evidence, not proof. Choose the sector responsible for the selected coded issue, not the delivery method or strongest unrelated clause. Water, soap, aquatabs, disinfectant and hand-washing equipment/stations: WASH. Medicines, treatment availability and access to clinical care: Health or Clinical care. Vaccines: Vaccination. General disease information, rumours, beliefs and unspecified appreciation in this community-feedback workflow: RCCE/CEA. Actor roles/governance: Coordination. MHPSS requires explicit psychosocial support, not merely courage or thanks. Logistics requires an explicit transport/storage/supply-chain issue; amener or fournir alone does not make a health/WASH request Logistics. A real suspected case or death requiring an alert in this selected clause: Surveillance. This field suggests a routing destination. For a simple thank-you or acknowledgment during outreach, select RCCE/CEA even when the speaker names no sector. A request for a washbasin routes to WASH. Choose the responsible sector for a concrete safeguarding or security concern before considering routine community engagement.

The assigned path may be uncertain: treat it as provisional evidence, not proof. Positive: thanks, blessing, appreciation or encouragement. Negative: fear, dissatisfaction, mistrust, explicit denial, conspiracy or accusation, even calmly phrased. Neutral: ordinary information questions, requests or factual observations without emotion. Do not label simple affirmation of disease existence or religious interpretation Negative solely because it is a belief. Mixed only if both positive and negative tones occur within this selected clause; Unclear if insufficient evidence. Never borrow another Type's tone. An information question without expressed emotion is Neutral. Unclear is an allowed sentiment when tone alone is indeterminate.
